panels.visual: Princess Ariadne of Crete (long dark curls, red-and-blue Minoan dress) secretly meeting the young hero Theseus at night by the dark doorway of the Labyrinth, pressing a red ball of thread into his hands
panels.caption: Princess Ariadne of Crete helped Theseus beat the Minotaur.

speech.speaker: Ariadne
speech.text: Tie it at the door. Follow it back.

panels.visual: Theseus bursting out of the Labyrinth doorway holding the red thread, sword in hand, Ariadne running to him
panels.caption: Her thread led him out of the Labyrinth alive.

panels.visual: Ariadne and Theseus on the deck of a ship slipping out of the harbour of Crete at dawn, hand in hand, Cretan palace behind them
panels.caption: She gave up her home and sailed away with him.

panels.visual: The ship pulling up on a quiet island beach with rocks and a little white chapel-like rock on a headland, sunset
panels.caption: They stopped for the night on the island of Naxos.

panels.visual: Ariadne asleep on the sand under a cloak in moonlight; Theseus tiptoeing away towards the ship, looking back guiltily
panels.caption: While she slept, Theseus crept back to the ship.

panels.visual: Ariadne waking at dawn on the empty beach, the ship tiny on the horizon, her hand reaching out
panels.caption: She woke up alone. His ship was already far away.

panels.visual: Ariadne standing on a rock in the wind, hair and dress whipping, shouting a curse at the sea with storm clouds gathering over the distant ship, dramatic
panels.caption: One old poem says she cursed him: may you forget, the way you forgot me.

panels.visual: The distant ship in a storm of grey cloud, its sail black; Theseus on deck looking blank and forgetful, a little question mark over his head
panels.caption: And Theseus forgot to change his black sails. You know what happened to his father.

panels.visual: The god Dionysus (young, long dark curls, ivy crown, leopard skin) arriving on the beach in a chariot pulled by two panthers, with dancing Bacchae women and music, grapevines sprouting from the sand
panels.caption: Then a god came to Naxos: Dionysus, with his panthers and his wild Bacchae.

panels.visual: Dionysus kneeling and offering his hand to the surprised Ariadne, petals and ivy swirling, warm golden light
panels.caption: He fell in love with her at first sight, and they married.

panels.visual: Dionysus throwing a glittering golden crown up into the night sky, where it turns into a curved arc of seven stars; Ariadne watching in wonder
panels.caption: As a wedding gift he threw her crown into the sky.

panels.visual: A modern night sky full of stars over the sea, a curved half-circle of bright stars highlighted with a faint dotted outline of a crown, a girl and an owl looking up from a rock
panels.caption: It is still there: the Northern Crown, Corona Borealis. Look for it on a summer night.
